understanding.goal_understanding: The goal was to complete each KA59 level by moving the available selectable piece(s) so that every goal tile marked with a '+' in the semantic grid was simultaneously occupied by a selectable piece; achieving WIN on the final level would complete the whole run.
understanding.mechanics_understanding: Movement used MOVE_LEFT/RIGHT/UP/DOWN to shift the currently selected piece in 3-pixels-per-cell increments on a grid, with walls/boundaries blocking or otherwise altering movement. Blocks could be pushable when directly adjacent in the movement direction, causing them to move along with the selected piece if space allowed. Some wall-like objects could behave inconsistently, so attempted moves were used to learn their true blocking behavior. When multiple selectables existed, control could be switched using CLICK with the exact pixel/grid coordinates of the target selectable.

understanding.goal_understanding: The goal was to complete each KA59 level by moving the available selectable piece(s) so that every goal tile marked with a '+' in the semantic grid was simultaneously occupied by a selectable piece; achieving WIN on the final level would complete the whole run.
understanding.mechanics_understanding: Movement used MOVE_LEFT/RIGHT/UP/DOWN to shift the currently selected piece in 3-pixels-per-cell increments on a grid, with walls/boundaries blocking or otherwise altering movement. Blocks could be pushable when directly adjacent in the movement direction, causing them to move along with the selected piece if space allowed. Some wall-like objects could behave inconsistently, so attempted moves were used to learn their true blocking behavior. When multiple selectables existed, control could be switched using CLICK with the exact pixel/grid coordinates of the target selectable.
